paragraphs.text: At the passover especially; for this and the other hallelujatical psalms that follow (called by the Jews the Great Hallelujah) were sung at that and other solemn feasts, in praise of God for his manifold mercies.

Musica huius Psalmi in signis est, siquis eam consequi potuit. The great art used in the composure of this and some other psalms (after the order of the Hebrew alphabet) serveth both to set forth their excellence and for the help of memory.
Magnalia; no small things are done by so great a hand. Grandior solet esse Deus in parvulis quam in magnis; in formicis maior anima quam in elephantis, in nanis quam in gigantibus.
paragraphs.anchor: The works of the Lord are great

paragraphs.text: q.d. Great though they be, yet are they seriously sought into and found out by those that delight therein; and the deeper they dive into them the sweeter they find them. Basil diligently described many creatures; and so did Ambrose after him. Pliny (who was himself a very great searcher in nature’s secrets) telleth of one who spent eight and fifty years in learning the nature of the bee, Et nondum assecutus sit onmia, and yet could not attain to all. Our anatomists find still new wonders in the body of a man, &c. God hath showed singular skill in his works, that men might admire him; but woe to such as regard not his handiwork, Isa 5:12.
Heb. honour and glory, they all come tipped and gilt, with a glory upon them, a centro ad coelum. This the brutish man knoweth not, Psa 92:6.
His judgments are sometimes secret, but always just.
Memorabilia reddidit mirabilia sua clemens et misericors Iehova.
Heb. a prey, Escam demensam; as he did manna to the Israelites, to each a homer; so to all his he giveth food convenient for them, Pro 30:8, Cibum et potum, quae sunt divitiae Christianorum (Jerome).
To pass by his people’s sins, and to supply all their necessities; all his paths to such are not mercy only, but truth, Psa 25:10
paragraphs.anchor: He will ever be mindful of his covenant

paragraphs.text: To them it is given to see, but not to others who are delivered up to a judiciary blindness. "Call unto me, and I will answer thee, and show thee great and hidden things which thou knowest not," Jer 33:3.
Yea, power over all nations, Rev 2:26
They speak him a true and just God. Chrysostom taketh truth here for mercy, and noteth that God usually mixeth mercy with justice; yet sometimes he sendeth an evil, an only evil, Eze 7:5
That is, his promises added to his commandments; or they are so called, because firm and sure, as the commandments of an emperor.
The promises are infallible, good sure hold, not yea and nay, but yea and amen.
paragraphs.anchor: They stand fast for ever and ever

paragraphs.text: i.e. Ordained, made, and ratified.
Once out of Egypt, ever out of Satan’s thraldom.
paragraphs.anchor: He sent redemption unto his people

paragraphs.text: Sic cum populo suo pactus est ut de ipsius paeti observatione certis edictis caverit, as he covenanted, so he looketh his commandments should be respected, which are as binding to us as his covenant is to him; and, through grace, his covenant is as binding to him as those are to us.
paragraphs.anchor: He hath commanded his covenant for ever

paragraphs.text: Which, therefore, we should not presume in a sudden unmannerliness to blurt out. The Jews would not pronounce it. The Grecians (as Suidas observeth), when they would swear by their Jupiter, forbare to mention him. This is cheek to the profaneness common among us. Let those that would have their name reverend labour to be holy as God is holy.
paragraphs.anchor: Holy and reverend is his name

paragraphs.text: Or the principal point and chief perfection. See Pro 1:7 Job 28:28. {See Trapp on "Pro 1:7"} {See Trapp on "Job 28:28"}
paragraphs.anchor: The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom

paragraphs.text: So much a man knoweth in true account, as he doth; hence understanding is here ascribed to the will; so Job 28:28. See Ecc 10:2. Some render it, Good success.
paragraphs.anchor: A good understanding have all they

paragraphs.text: i.e. God’s praise; for they that understand it of the godly wise man understand not the propriety of the Hebrew word Tehillah, saith an interpreter.
